reads: github:issues and their body edit history

name: plan
intent: Compile issue-dag/2 frontmatter from GitHub into a reduced DAG, rank the open frontier and propose a conflict-free batch (read-only; --from-github)

reads: github:issues and their body edit history

name: edit
intent: Add or remove one edge in a child issue's frontmatter .blocked_by, then recompile; an added edge is restored when the run fails (--add-edge, --remove-edge)

reads: github:issues and their body edit history

name: verify
intent: Compile a hand-written DAG specification and rank it (read-only; --verify-dag)

name: inventory
intent: List worktrees, unmerged branches, open pull requests and open issues of a repository (read-only, fail-closed). Inventory applies no trust gate: strangers' titles, authors and branch names are listed as data

schema.title: Taskalisk plan summary
schema.description: The first result of a plan: the smallest line that answers 'what next'. It names the frontier and the batch in rank order, the outcome, the metrics, the trust in force and the artifact hash. Detail follows on later lines.

outcome.description: compiled: the graph was ranked; cycle or unresolved: it could not be, and no frontier, batch or metrics follow.

ok.description: True only when the plan compiled and the run reports no error. False means do not dispatch from it; the error lines say why.

error_codes.description: The codes of the parley.error lines this run reports, in the order they follow.

artifact_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical result document (sorted keys, compact separators, trailing LF), the same value the 1.x compiler printed as meta.artifact_hash.

frontier.description: Wave 0 in rank order; one taskalisk.frontier_node line follows for each.

batch.description: The conflict-free batch in rank order; taskalisk.batch carries its detail.

schema.title: Taskalisk finding
schema.description: One thing the compile found that a reader should see: a violation, a warning, an untrusted or unmodeled issue, an opaque blocker, a not-planned parent, a redundant edge and the like. code is stable; message is a sentence built from trusted data only.

run.description: The execution this line belongs to (Parley spec 2.1).

code.description: Stable codes: frontmatter.violation: An issue's frontmatter breaks the issue-dag/2 rules; subject is the issue, message the rule. frontmatter.warning: A frontmatter value is allowed but suspicious (for example .size_hours above 8). issue.untrusted: An issue failed the trust gate (C1): listed, never a node unless a trusted issue references it, and then only as an opaque blocker. detail: id, url, state, author, reasons, referenced_by. No title. pull_request.untrusted: A pull request that closes a task is not from a same-repository branch by a trusted author (C4); it has no effect. detail: number, url, author, cross_repository, closes, reason. issue.unmodeled: An open home issue has no frontmatter; it is not a node. detail: id, title, url. issue.opaque: A referenced issue has no frontmatter; it blocks its dependents and is never dispatched. detail: id, title, state, referenced_by. container.excluded: A container groups issues and is not itself a node. detail: id, number, title. parent.not_planned: A blocker closed as not planned still satisfies the edge; review it. detail: parent, child, title. edge.redundant: A declared edge is implied by a longer path and left out of the reduced graph. detail: from, to, implied_via. edge.soft_or_low_confidence: A --verify-dag edge that is soft or below --min-confidence; not in the graph. detail: from, to, type, isHard, confidence, evidence. prerequisite.unknown: A node names a prerequisite that is neither open nor completed. detail: node, unknown_prerequisite. prerequisite.stale_merged_hint: A --verify-dag prerequisite marked (merged) is still open. detail: node, prerequisite, prerequisite_status. graph.cyclic_node: A node on or behind a cycle of hard edges. relationship.only_in_frontmatter: With --compare-relationships: an edge in frontmatter that GitHub's blocked_by relationships lack. detail: from, to. relationship.only_in_github: With --compare-relationships: a GitHub blocked_by relationship that frontmatter lacks. detail: from, to. since_last.no_previous: With --since-last: no earlier completed receipt of this tool in this working directory asked the same question, so nothing was compared.

schema.title: parley run bootstrap
schema.description: First line of stdout, emitted before work begins so a crashed run still names its receipt.

seq.description: The bootstrap line is always the first line the run emits, so it is the only line with a pinned seq.

v.description: The program's own version, distinct from _schema.version on the same line (spec §3).

inv.description: Content-addressed identity of the question: tool, version, normalised args, and the bytes of every declared input; never a declared secret (spec §2.2, §5.3). Optional in v0.2: supplied when the tool documents its derivation and the identity is known at this point; never a placeholder (spec §2.2).

run.description: Unique, lexicographically sortable identity of this execution.

session.description: Working period spanning runs. Supplied by the caller or inherited.

receipt.description: Absolute path of the receipt file for this run (spec §5). The only path the protocol defines; a program may add others it documents.

dry_run.description: True when the run performed no subject-matter writes, no mutating remote action and no retention deletion (spec §4.3). Absent means false.

schema.title: parley receipt head
schema.description: First line of a receipt file. Carries what the bootstrap line deliberately omitted, so stdout stays small while the record stays complete.

seq.description: The run's single counter continues from the bootstrap line, which is seq 0 (spec §1.3).

run.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1). ULID or equivalent: unique per execution and lexicographically sortable.

tool.description: The program that wrote this receipt, so a receipt read alone says what produced it (spec §5).

v.description: That program's own version; with tool, a component of the inv preimage (spec §2.2) that a receipt read alone must carry.

inv.description: Content-addressed identity of the question (spec §2.2); never includes a declared secret. Optional in v0.2: supplied when the tool documents its derivation and the identity is known at this point; never a placeholder (spec §2.2).

argv.description: As received, after §5.3 redaction: a declared secret appears as the literal [redacted].

resolved.description: After defaults, environment and path resolution. The gap between this and argv is where bugs live.

inputs.description: Every declared input as a descriptor: its path, its role when the tool distinguishes roles, and a content digest once read. A digest that arrives later is carried by receipt.inputs (spec §2.2). Credential files are never inputs (§2.2).

error.description: Why the input could not be read; no digest then.
